about.title: Vacaville Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product can turn an ordinary afternoon in Vacaville into a hospital visit. It might be a power tool that kicks back in a garage off Peabody Road, a space heater that ignites in a home near Alamo Drive, a child's car seat that fails on I-80, or a medication with a warning label that left out something important. California treats these cases differently from most injury claims. Under strict liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product was defective in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach the maker, the distributor, and the store on Nut Tree Road that sold it. Solano County juries hear these cases, and the physical product is usually the most important piece of evidence, so hold onto it. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect Vacaville residents with an independent attorney who handles product cases on contingency, and the connection costs you nothing.

items.question: Do I need to prove the company was careless to win a product liability case in California?
items.answer: Usually not. California applies strict liability to most defective product claims, which means you generally need to show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Negligence can still be argued, but it is often not required. An attorney can explain which theory fits your situation.

items.question: A car part failed while I was driving on I-80 near Vacaville. Is that a product case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Vacaville recorded 335 injury collisions in 2025, and some crashes involve equipment that did not perform as designed, such as airbags, tires, or brakes. If a defective component contributed to your injuries, the manufacturer or seller may be liable alongside any at-fault driver. Keep the vehicle and the part intact so they can be inspected.

items.question: I threw away the product that injured me. Can I still bring a claim?
items.answer: It is harder, but not always impossible. Photos, receipts, medical records, the packaging, and the same model purchased elsewhere can sometimes fill the gap. Do not discard anything else connected to the incident, and speak with an attorney soon so remaining evidence can be preserved. LawProactive can make that connection for free.
